difficulty_reason: R_u is smooth over k(u) hence finite-dimensional while dim_u(U) may be infinite, giving values in Z ∪ {∞}; for a second presentation form P = U x_X U', pick p over (u,u') by points-cartesian, apply the smoothness dimension formula twice to get dim_p(P) expressed through both presentations; identify R'_{u'} with the base change of P_u over the common field Omega via the 2-morphism of the two compositions (mechanism described in-span with the Omega-point correspondence, some details omitted), conclude dim equality by the dimension-fibre-after-base-change lemma and symmetry.
